title: Integrable majorants and the norm of an integral
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $F:X\to\mathbf C$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable (equal almost everywhere to a pointwise limit of measurable simple functions), and let $G:X\to\mathbf R$ be Lebesgue integrable. If $|F(x)|\leq G(x)$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$, then $F$ is Lebesgue integrable and $$\left|\int_X F\,d\mu\right|\leq\int_X G\,d\mu.$$ The measure $\mu$ may in particular be a measure restricted to a measurable subset.
